gui.intel_corrupted_msg:
Detected that your CPU is affected by a critical Intel chip bug.

If you are not familiar with this issue, it is highly recommended to read this $LINK.INTEL_CHIP_BUG_FAQ$. DO NOT report this crash until you have:
  • Updated your BIOS.
  • Made sure that the crash is not caused by this bug, as the issue won't be resolved even after a BIOS update if the CPU has already started dying. It is important to note that this update will not fix damaged hardware. If the PC has crashed or been unstable due to this issue, the CPU is damaged.
  • If the CPU is damaged, replace it under warranty. Intel has extended the warranty for affected processors by two years.
This warning doesn't indicate that this crash is 100% caused by this issue, but before reporting, you must check that a corrupted CPU is not the reason.

warnings.jemalloc: The jemalloc "Problematic frame" in $LOG_FILENAME$ indicates an issue with the jemalloc memory allocator. To resolve this, add the following argument to your JVM args: -Dorg.lwjgl.system.allocator=system
warnings.jvm: The jvm.dll "Problematic frame" in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file may result from various issues, including a hardware bug or a bug in the JVM itself. Please try the following steps in order: $FIRST_PRIORITY_WARNINGS$1) Have you seen our warning about Intel 13th and 14th‑generation processors? If you’ve experienced any system instability (BSODs, random app crashes), this is likely the cause. 2) If memory overclocking (XMP/DOCP/EXPO) is enabled, disable it, as it doesn’t seem to work well with your system and may be causing memory corruption. Look for memeory diagnostics instructions in the buttom of this message. 3) Apply the recommended JVM arguments for your modpack. 4) Test different Java versions or vendors, as the bug may come from the current JVM installation version or vendor. 5) Try reducing active CPU count like this, via JVM argument: -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=$HALF_OF_PROCESSORS$ 6) If none of the above helps, contact support. Memory diagnostics instructions: 1) Save this $LINK.RESULTS_OF_MEMORY_DIAGNOSTICS$. It will be needed to get results of diagnostics after reboot. 2) Press win + R to open the Run dialog box, enter mdsched and click OK. 3) In the Windows Memory Diagnostic window, click the Restart now and check for problems option. If you don’t see a popup with the results after reboot, refer to the instructions on how to view them. Please note: this test may not detect every memory issue, and it won’t confirm if the JVM crash is 100% caused by memory. Disabling memory overclocking is still the best first step.

warnings.macjdk: The v ~StubRoutines::SafeFetch32 "Problematic Frame" error in $LOG_FILENAME$ is caused by an issue with the bundled Java runtime ("Microsoft" build version 17.0.8 and newer) on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/etc.) CPUs, which causes Java to crash under certain conditions. To resolve this issue, you first need to install a different Java runtime: 1. Click $LINK.AZUL_DOWNLOAD$ to get the recommended Java version for your system. 2. Hover the Download button and click ".dmg" to download the installer. 3. Open the downloaded file and follow the installation instructions. Next, you need to configure your Minecraft launcher to use the newly installed Java. The following instructions are for $LINK.ATL$ and may vary for other launchers: 1. Click "Settings" on the right. 2. Select "Java/Minecraft" at the top. 3. Uncheck "Use Java Provided by Minecraft". 4. Manually enter the following Java path in the "Java Install Location" text box: /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/zulu-21.jdk/Contents/Home/bin/java
warnings.lib_gl_programmability: The libGLProgrammability.dylib “Problematic frame” in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file is caused by a bug in Apple’s in‑house OpenGL driver, this blocks many advanced shader packs from working on macOS. Apple makes all the drivers in‑house; fixes only arrive via macOS updates. Most likely you are using an incompatible shader pack with macOS. Disable shaders or switch to a shader pack compatible with macOS. Note: This has been an issue since 2021, so it’s most likely still not fixed.
warnings.insufficient_memory: The There is insufficient memory... message in the $LOG_FILENAME$ file means: Your system is running out of available physical RAM or swap space. To fix this: $FIRST_PRIORITY_WARNINGS$1) Make sure your memory isn't heavily used by other running applications — check using Task Manager, and try to keep unnecessary programs closed while playing Minecraft. 2) Ensure you are using the recommended memory settings for this modpack — perhaps your Xmx value is set too high? 3) If you followed some dumb internet advices about disabling page files, revert it — that's likely the cause. Even if you have, say, 128 GB of RAM and most of it is free, Java still needs swap space to function properly. Look for instructions how to check/enable page files in the bottom of the message. 4) Check your disk space. If you're running out of it, there might not be enough space for the swap area, so you'll need to free up some space to fix the issue. 5) Sometimes, simply restarting your computer can help clear out memory and reset swap usage. 6) If you're using more than the recommended memory settings for this pack, try lowering them. 7) If none of this helps $END_RECOMMENDATIONS$ How To Check/Enable/Change Paging File Size: 1) From the Windows search button search up "Advanced System Settings" and open the first result. 2)Press the "Settings" button located under the Performance section. 3)In the new section that has opened press "Advanced" and after press the "Change" button located under the "Virtual Memory" section. 4)Check "automatically manage paging file size for all drivers" checkbox.

warnings.closed_by_windows: If this crash happened during game or level loading, or while closing the game, it was likely caused by pressing keys or clicking the mouse. The error "The program javaw.exe version ... stopped interacting with Windows and was closed" in $LOG_FILENAME$ means the game froze, possibly due to these actions. To avoid this, let the game load/close fully—DO NOT CLICK ANYTHING, PRESS ANY KEY, or CLICK END PROCESS. If the crash occurred during mid-gameplay, just press OK and ignore this message.
warnings.curseforge_corrupted: We detected signs in the $LOG_FILENAME$ that your Minecraft installation is corrupted by CurseForge. To fix it, follow the steps below: 1. warnings.java_too_high: We detected signs in the $LOG_FILENAME$ that this crash is caused by too high Java version: $JAVA_VERSION$ To fix it, use the recommended Java version for this version of Minecraft.
warnings.resource_location_exception: We detected signs in $LOG_FILENAME$ that your game encountered a resource location error: $LINE_FROM_LOG$. This typically happens when Minecraft tries to load a resource (such as a block, item, or texture) using a name that contains invalid characters. This is most often caused by one of the following reasons: 1) Non-English system language settings. In such cases, the resource location may include a Unicode symbol in this format: \u0131n. To fix this, add the following JVM arguments to force the game to use English locale settings: -Duser.language=en -Duser.region=US 2) A mod has incorrectly handled a resource location. Try removing the mod that added this faulty resource. It is strongly recommended to try the first solution before resorting to the second one.

warnings.c6a: We detected signs in $LOG_FILENAME$ of missing Create mod classes, while the Create mod is currently installed. Create Update 6 was released recently, and you may have one of the following mismatches: - Create Update 5 with addons for Update 6, or - Create Update 6 with addons for Update 5. (Addons here refer to any mod that integrates with Create, including both standard addons and mods with Create compatibility.) You'll need to ensure that all Create-related mods are either from Update 5 or Update 6. Note that release dates are not a fully reliable way to determine compatibility. This may be a false alarm, so please double-check. To identify which mods are incompatible with your current version of the Create mod: Click OK, then open on top of the window $LANG.gui.menu.analysis$ -> $LANG.gui.menu.analysis.create_dependencies$. warnings.ctov_without_lithostitched:
Detected that you are using the CTOV (ChoiceTheorem's Overhauled Village) mod without $LINK.LITHOSTITCHED$.
Technically, CTOV will work on its own, but as soon as other mods are involved, it stops working.
If your modpack includes many mods, this is most likely the issue, and installing $LINK.LITHOSTITCHED$ should fix it.
warnings.duplicated_mods: At the end of $LOG_FILENAME$, we found an error about duplicated mods: $LINE_FROM_LOG$ To fix this crash, keep only one of the mods listed above.
warnings.modernifx_watchdog: At the end of $LOG_FILENAME$, we found a message from the IntegratedWatchdog about one server tick took way longer than it should have: $LINE_FROM_LOG$ If you weren’t doing something extremely slow, like using WorldEdit to change trillions of blocks, this likely means the Integrated Server has deadlocked. A deadlock happens when parts of the game are waiting on each other in a way that prevents anything from continuing — like a traffic jam where every car is blocking another. To fix this crash, check the thread dump at the end of the log. It shows which parts of the game were waiting on each other. This can be hard to understand without technical knowledge. You can try using some advanced reasoning AI tool to analyze the thread dump — it may help identify the mod causing the issue. If this happened in an unmodified modpack, please report it to the developers — it shouldn’t happen.
warnings.optifine: Once upon a time, OptiFine was the go-to solution to make your game better, faster, and stronger through various useful features and optimizations. But things have changed. Other open-source projects offer better performance, significantly improved compatibility, and full shader support. warnings_common.drivers: You (likely) need to update your graphics drivers in order to resolve the crash. Here's how to go about doing that! 1. Identify your graphics card Your current GPU used to run this instance of Minecraft is: $CURRENT_GPU$ if you already know skip to the next step - Open task manager - Navigate to the "Performance" tab (on Windows 11 this is the button that looks like a heart pulse) - Press the GPU 0 graph and read your GPU from the top right Note: In some cases you may see a GPU 0 and GPU 1. This means your CPU has its own GPU, as well as a dedicated one. You probably want GPU 1 (which is usually the better one), but you can ask staff to clarify if necessary. 2. Download your drivers from the manufacturers site Depending on what you read before, you likely need drivers from either AMD, Intel, or NVIDIA AMD: $LINK.AMD_SUPPORT$ Intel: $LINK.INTEL_DRIVERS$ NVIDIA: $LINK.NVIDIA_DRIVERS$ Note: - For NVIDIA you want to select "Game Ready Driver (GRD)" (this is the default option) for the best performance. Once installing you'd probably prefer downloading GeForce Experience, which will notify you when there's an available drivers update. - For Intel, you probably want to press "Get Started" under the "Automatically update your drivers and software", which will simplify the process and update everything automatically. - For AMD you probably want to just press "Download Windows Drivers", which will download something called AMD Adrenaline, which will update your drivers automatically. 3. Run the installation, restart your computer, and try playing MC again - At this point, hopefully your Minecraft is running. If it still does not work, contact support with report from $LANG.gui.upload_all_comment$ button.

gui.privacy.title: Privacy Information
gui.privacy.mclogs_privacy_info:
Privacy Policy

Crash Assistant

Crash Assistant is a Minecraft mod that processes your personal data (such as logs) entirely locally on your PC, limited to what is necessary to provide the functionality described in the $LINK.CRASH_ASSISTANT$. Crash Assistant itself is entirely client-side—it has no servers and never receives a copy of your logs. If you don't want Crash Assistant to process your personal data even locally, close it and remove it from the mods folder. Crash Assistant is created by KostromDan. You can contact me on my $LINK.CRASH_ASSISTANT_DISCORD$. Furthermore, according to §77 GDPR, you have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority if you believe that the processing of your personal data is illicit. The following sections describe the log-upload functionality provided by Crash Assistant.

mclo.gs

Logs are uploaded only when you explicitly click one of the "Upload" buttons, and they are sent directly to mclo.gs, a log-sharing service operated by Aternos GmbH (Germany). Before publishing, mclo.gs automatically tries to redact sensitive information—such as access tokens, IP addresses, or computer usernames—to keep your paste safe to share. However, mclo.gs cannot guarantee that this always works. This is not anonymising! Only data that can be used to harm you is tried to be removed. Minecraft usernames, UUIDs, and other identifying information are retained. Complete information on retention periods, access rights, data redaction, contact details and your GDPR rights is available in their $LINK.MCLOGS_PRIVACY_POLICY$.

gnomebot.dev

Because the mobile UI of mclo.gs can be inconvenient, Crash Assistant—by default—wraps the returned URL through gnomebot.dev (e.g. https://mclo.gs/X → https://gnomebot.dev/paste/mclogs/X). You can disable this behaviour in the settings. Currently enabled: $GNOMEBOT_ENABLED$ gnomebot.dev is an open-source online log viewer; it fetches data from mclo.gs, displays it with convenient formatting, and caches the paste in RAM for five minutes after the last access before discarding it. gnomebot.dev is created by Latvian Modder. You can contact him on his $LINK.LAT_DISCORD$.

Consent Validity

By clicking Accept in the dialog before uploading a log, you give your consent to the processing of your data for the purpose of uploading logs. We(Crash Assistant) process your data only on the basis of your freely given consent. If the checkbox $LANG.gui.privacy.remember_my_choice$ is selected, your consent will be stored locally on your PC in the "local/crash_assistant/local_config.json" path, relative to folder of this modpack and remains valid as long as that folder exists or until you revoke your consent. If the checkbox is not selected, consent remains valid only until the GUI is closed or the consent is revoked.

Consent Reset

To withdraw your consent, open the menu $LANG.gui.menu.privacy$ → $LANG.gui.menu.privacy.reset_consent$ at any time. Warning: withdrawing your consent only revokes permission to upload logs. You will need to grant consent again before uploading logs in the future. This action does not remove logs that have already been uploaded to mclo.gs; you must contact them directly for deletion.

Upload Volume

You decide which logs to upload and for what purpose. Clicking the $LANG.gui.upload_and_copy_link_button$ button next to a single entry sends only that specific log. Clicking $LANG.gui.upload_all_button$ sends every log listed under $LANG.gui.file_list_label$ plus the mods-difference file. The copied message may contain additional context — please review it before sharing.
